first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ, both plausibly linked since onboarding friction suppresses downstream activation. Two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) converge on signup/onboarding simplification producing durable activation and completion lifts for SMB/self-serve accounts, with no noted retention harm—unlike promotional pricing (memory_73), which is explicitly flagged as damaging 30-day retention despite competitive pressure from the rival's pricing move. Chasing price-sensitive SMBs via discounting risks repeating a known retention failure and conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable alternative but addresses a narrower symptom (week-one engagement) rather than the upstream onboarding completion drop. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are unrelated to the current acute declines. I want to verify the two onboarding memories before committing the single weekly experiment slot to ensure the original effect sizes and conditions still justify a standard-scale test rather than a broad rollout, since I have not previously confirmed these against archived source records.
